title: Odile and the Ember
premise: Noor Sandoval has survived twenty years in the city of Vell by hiding her beast-speaker gift behind harmless charms, until the old gods stir beneath the mountain and begin answering prayers with terrible bargains. When a street child she loves is taken as payment for the Ember—a stolen fragment of divine fire held by the court beneath the mountain—Noor must ally with an exiled god's last priest and a disgraced city magistrate to steal the child's soul back. Infiltrating the court, Noor discovers the Ember itself is a caged god who has been feeding on sold souls to survive, and that her own gift was seeded by it long ago. She chooses to shatter the Ember rather than claim its power, freeing the souls and scattering the old gods back into the world—wild, unowned, and no longer for sale—at the cost of her own invisibility and nearly her life.
about_author: F. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal fishing villages before turning to fiction. They write about magic that refuses to be owned, and live quietly with too many houseplants and one opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Price of Small Wonders
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet Noor selling charms in Vell's night market, hiding her true gift even from her found family of market strays, including twelve-year-old Tam. When prayers at the old shrine start being answered—too literally—and a neighbor's wish costs him his voice, Noor realizes the gods have woken. The beat: dread disguised as ordinary life, ending when Tam prays for his sick mother and something answers.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Owes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with interludes from Magistrate Ilsa Vane, who has been quietly investigating soul-ledgers. Tam vanishes; a black receipt stamped with the mountain seal names him payment. Noor seeks out Brother Cassian, last priest of the shattered god, who reveals the Ember beneath the court feeds on sold souls—and that Noor's gift marks her as connected to it. Beat: grief hardening into resolve as unlikely allies form outside the law.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Noor, Cassian, and Vane descend through the mountain's bone-roads into the court, where the Ember sits enthroned among centuries of harvested souls. Noor speaks with beasts of the deep dark to pass its wards, but the Ember recognizes her gift as its own seed and offers her power in exchange for Tam's soul kept. Vane is captured buying their way past the gate. Beat: temptation at full strength—the climax where Noor refuses and shatters the Ember.

chapters.title: Ashes That Answer
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The Ember breaks; souls pour free, including Tam's, though he returns changed and slow to remember her. The old gods scatter into the wild, answerable to no bargain now, and Vane burns the soul-ledgers publicly while Cassian begins teaching prayer without price. Noor, exposed and hunted by the court's remnants, finds her found family standing openly beside her. Beat: bittersweet resolution—justice won outside the law, belonging chosen over safety.
